title: Ukrainian Drone Strikes Cut 30% of Russian Refining Capacity, X-Energy Wins an NRC Permit for Four Texas Modular Reactors, and US Gasoline Falls Below $4 a Gallon
subhead: Western and Ukrainian assessments indicate that long-range drone strikes have knocked out roughly 30 percent of Russia's oil refining capacity as 146 drones targeted the Leningrad region near Baltic export ports; the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission granted X-energy a construction permit to build four small modular nuclear reactors in Texas; and average US retail gasoline prices dropped below $4 per gallon for the first time since July following a 9-million-barrel weekly crude inventory build.

sections.heading: Ukrainian Strikes Knock Out 30% of Russian Refining Capacity and Target Baltic Ports
sections.body:
Sustained Ukrainian long-range unmanned aerial attacks against Russian downstream energy infrastructure have reduced Russia's national oil refining processing capacity by approximately 30 percent, according to official assessments released as US-mediated peace talks entered their second day in Abu Dhabi (The Independent). Overnight into Wednesday, Russian air defense authorities claimed the interception of 141 to 146 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones over the Leningrad region, triggering security alerts around Russia's primary Baltic Sea crude and product export terminals (Al Jazeera, Dünya).

The concentrated campaign against Russian distillation units and Baltic export hubs has forced Moscow to divert additional crude volumes toward sea-borne export terminals even as Western sanctions enforcement tightens across the North Atlantic. Energy analysts noted that losing nearly a third of domestic refining throughput constrains Russian diesel and aviation fuel supply for both domestic industrial users and military logistics ahead of peak winter demand (The Independent, Dünya).
sections.whyItMatters: Taking 30 percent of Russia's refining capacity offline while threatening Baltic Sea export terminals gives Kyiv direct economic leverage over Moscow's export revenues during the Abu Dhabi ceasefire talks.

sections.heading: X-Energy Wins NRC Permit for Four Texas Modular Reactors as Senate Advances Permitting Bill
sections.body:
Advanced nuclear developer X-energy received a construction permit from the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to build four small modular nuclear reactors (SMRs) in Texas, marking a major regulatory milestone for commercial fourth-generation high-temperature gas-cooled reactors in the United States (TechCrunch). The four-reactor complex will supply zero-carbon industrial process heat and baseload electricity along the Texas Gulf Coast.

On Capitol Hill, the US Senate took another procedural step Tuesday night to advance bipartisan energy and infrastructure permitting legislation toward final passage in the upper chamber, aiming to lock in faster federal approvals for transmission lines, pipelines, and nuclear projects before the incoming Democratic-majority Congress takes office in January (The Hill, OilPrice). Simultaneously, major oil and gas operators are expanding into domestic battery minerals, led by commercial direct-lithium-extraction investments in a high-concentration Arkansas Smackover brine formation described by geologists as a 'geologic freak' (OilPrice).
sections.whyItMatters: NRC construction approval for X-energy's four Texas reactors moves US small modular nuclear power from design licensing into physical construction just as industrial and data center buyers seek 24/7 carbon-free power.

sections.heading: US Gasoline Drops Below $4 on 9M-Barrel Crude Build as Hormuz and Houthi Attacks Persist
sections.body:
Average retail gasoline prices across the United States fell to $3.98 per gallon on Tuesday—dropping below the $4.00 mark for the first time since July—after global crude prices shed more than 11 percent over the past week and seasonal driving demand eased (Anadolu Agency, Bloomberg HT, Proactive Investors). Adding to the bearish domestic supply picture, the American Petroleum Institute (API) reported a sharp 9.0-million-barrel build in US commercial crude oil inventories for the week ending November 6, reversing the prior week's 5.27-million-barrel drawdown, while North Dakota regulators projected rising Bakken oilfield activity in the second half of the year (OilPrice, EnergyNow).

Despite signs of physical oversupply and vessel-tracking data showing overall Strait of Hormuz oil flows recovering close to pre-war levels, localized security incidents prompted crude futures to edge up from two-month lows on Wednesday morning (OilPrice, Reuters, Wall Street Journal). The UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency reported a fresh security incident involving a commercial tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, while Yemen's Houthi movement announced another long-range missile and drone salvo targeting pumping stations along Saudi Arabia's crucial East-West crude pipeline (Anadolu Agency, Reuters, OilPrice). In East Africa, landlocked South Sudan began courting foreign investors for 14 oil exploration blocks to lift output from 170,000 to 230,000 barrels per day despite warring factions in neighboring Sudan taking a cut of transit flows, while Canada reinstated sanctions on 11 Iranian energy, banking, and shipping entities (OilPrice, Bloomberg HT).
sections.whyItMatters: A 9-million-barrel US crude inventory build and sub-$4 gasoline prices show that rebounding Persian Gulf exports are outweighing episodic Houthi missile salvos and Hormuz shipping incidents in physical balances.

sections.heading: Turkey Pushes '35 by 35' Electrification Pledge at COP31 as IAG Warns on Green Aviation Costs
sections.body:
At the inaugural Global Electrification Forum during the COP31 summit in Antalya, host Turkey urged nearly 200 participating nations to back its flagship '35 by 35' initiative—a global pledge to raise electricity's share of final energy consumption from roughly 20 percent today to 35 percent by 2035 (OilPrice, Anadolu Agency, Habertürk). Turkish Deputy Energy Minister Zafer Demircan emphasized investments in cross-border grid interconnections, distribution networks, and domestic clean energy manufacturing, though climate negotiators noted that Ankara's proposed declaration focuses on grid expansion rather than binding fossil-fuel consumption cuts (OilPrice, Anadolu Agency, Milliyet).

In European transport energy, International Airlines Group (IAG) CEO Luis Gallego—whose group owns British Airways and Iberia—warned that strict European Union and UK sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) mandates and environmental levies threaten to 'kill' European aviation competitiveness by driving up ticket prices relative to non-European hub carriers (OilPrice). Meanwhile, in critical clean-tech materials, Benchmark Mineral Intelligence projected that Japan will continue paying steep import premiums for yttrium through 2028 due to concentrated Chinese rare-earth processing controls (Benchmark Mineral Intelligence).
sections.whyItMatters: Turkey's '35 by 35' COP31 proposal reframes global climate diplomacy around grid electrification and cross-border transmission rather than fossil-fuel phaseout mandates, making it palatable to hydrocarbon-producing states.

bottomLine: Global energy markets balanced physical supply builds against persistent infrastructure strikes on Wednesday: average US retail gasoline prices fell below $4 per gallon for the first time since July following a 9-million-barrel API crude inventory build, even as oil futures bounced off two-month lows after a new tanker incident in the Strait of Hormuz, a Houthi missile salvo against Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, and Ukrainian drone strikes that have cut 30 percent of Russian refining capacity. In clean energy and regulation, X-energy won an NRC construction permit to build four small modular reactors in Texas, the US Senate advanced bipartisan permitting reform closer to passage, and host Turkey launched its '35 by 35' global electrification push at COP31 in Antalya.
sources: Reuters, Wall Street Journal, OilPrice, The Independent, Al Jazeera, The Hill, TechCrunch, Benchmark Mineral Intelligence, EnergyNow, Proactive Investors, Anadolu Agency, Bloomberg HT, Dünya, Habertürk, Milliyet
